transcript.content: Hello, thank you for coming in today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because my mood has been completely all over the place. For the past year, my emotions have been swinging back and forth constantly, but over the last month, I've fallen into a really severe, deep depression. It's just been incredibly exhausting to deal with this instability.

You mentioned your mood has been swinging back and forth. During the 'up' times, did you experience periods of extremely high energy, feeling on top of the world, or needing much less sleep than usual?

Yes, during those 'up' times, I felt completely on top of the world and had this overflowing energy where I just couldn't stay still. I felt extremely happy and full of vitality for no particular reason. However, I don't recall sleeping any less than usual during those periods.
How long do these high-energy 'up' periods typically last, and did they ever cause significant problems in your daily life or lead to hospitalization?

These high-energy periods have been happening on and off for about 12 months. During these times, my thoughts race and I'm constantly active, which definitely causes some disruption in my daily life. However, they have never been severe enough to lead to hospitalization.
Have you ever heard voices, seen things that others couldn't, or held strong beliefs that others found unusual, especially during times when your mood was normal?
No, I have never experienced anything like that. I've never heard voices, seen things that weren't there, or held any unusual beliefs.
When you have these high-energy 'up' periods, how many days in a row do they typically last?
I'm not entirely sure exactly how many days in a row they last. However, I have been experiencing these high-energy ups and downs on and off over the past year.
When you have these 'up' periods, do they typically last for at least four days in a row, or are they usually shorter than that?
Yes, they definitely last for at least four days in a row. In fact, these high periods usually last much longer than that, and it has been a recurring issue for about 12 months now.

When these high periods last longer, do they ever go on for a full week (7 days) or more? Also, during those times, did they cause major problems like getting into serious trouble at work or severely straining your relationships?

To be honest, I'm not entirely sure if those high periods ever lasted for a full seven days continuously. I also don't recall them causing any major trouble for me at work or leading to severe problems in my relationships.

During these high-energy times, did friends or family members ever comment that you were acting completely out of character, or did you find yourself doing impulsive things like spending too much money?
I don't recall anyone ever mentioning that I was acting out of character during those times. I also don't think I engaged in any impulsive behaviors, like reckless spending or anything like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient describes a current severe depressive episode lasting one month, alongside a 12-month history of recurrent 'up' periods characterized by elevated mood, increased energy, racing thoughts, and psychomotor agitation. These high periods last at least four days and do not cause severe social or occupational impairment or require hospitalization, which is characteristic of hypomanic episodes. This clinical picture supports Bipolar II Disorder.
